forecaster_note: Clean morning of head-high-plus surf at the S magnets. Lumpier but doable in the afternoon. A 6.3ft @ 11s S/SSE groundswell (169°) is the engine today, with a small 2.4ft @ 8s ENE (76°) underneath. Light W–WNW offshores hold until about 11am before the wind swings S and freshens to 18–19 km/h through the afternoon. Saturday repeats the pattern — clean-ish head-high+ at the S magnets in the morning, onshore and lumpy after midday — then Sunday eases back to a smaller, cleaner AM window. — Surfline Sydney Regional Forecast

wind.summary: WNW 7 km/h gusting 9 at dawn — genuine light offshore, holding W/SW to about 11am. Swings S from midday and builds to 18–19 km/h onshore by 2pm. The clean window is 6:20–11am, no exceptions.

shark.summary: SharkSmart NSW live: shark sighted by drone at Palm Beach 3:55pm yesterday (27 Aug) — water evacuated. That's ~20 km north of Dee Why and none of your four spots have a detection in the last 24 h. Feed is healthy (most recent statewide detection 0.7 h old, 12 in 24 h).

days.label: Today
days.note: Best morning of the run — 651 kJ of energy, 100/100 consistency and light WNW offshore until about 11am. The catch is direction: 6.3ft @ 11s from 169° is close to the dead-S angle that wraps badly at Dee Why, which is why Long Reef is 6–10ft and Manly is only 3–4ft. The 11s period is long enough to give it more shape than a raw wind swell. High tide 8:16am; wind swings S and ruins it by midday.

dee-why.window: 6:20–10:30am. Surfline has it Fair–Good right through the offshore block, easing to Fair once the S'ly arrives around 11am. High tide 8:16am — fish the push, then the first of the drop.
alerts: Primary swell at 169° is near the dead-S angle that wraps badly here — expect the bay to close out and the Point to carry the session
Wind swings S at 11am and hits 18 km/h onshore by 2pm

tip.label: Frontside at the Point, and go early
tip.text: 651 kJ with 100/100 consistency is a lot of energy — sets will keep coming, so patience at the Point pays. The 11s period on that S swell is the saving grace; it has enough wavelength to bend around and stand up rather than just close out like a 9s S would. The 2.4ft ENE at 76° sits in your 30–80° sweet spot but is too small to shape the session on its own. Sit up the Point, go frontside on the rights, use the push to the 8:16am high. Off the Point you're just paddling into shifting closeouts.

long-reef.window: 6:20–10am if you want the size. Offshore early, but Surfline drops it to Poor–Fair once the S'ly fills in.
alerts: Biggest of the four by a long way — 6–10ft converting the full S swell
Rating degrades to Poor–Fair from late morning

tip.label: The most wave, the least forgiveness
tip.text: The reef points straight into 169°, so it's taking the whole 6.3ft @ 11s and doubling it up. Well overhead with 651 kJ behind it is real surf — you're a strong paddler and it's inside your range, but it's a step-up board and a committed session, not a casual one. If you go, go at 6:20am while the WNW is still offshore and you have the whole tide push in front of you.

curl-curl.window: 6:20–10:30am. North Curly corner for the best shape and a bit of protection from the sweep.
alerts: Strong sweep likely with 6.3ft of S swell running the bank

tip.label: The middle option between Dee Why and Long Reef
tip.text: Curly is the classic S-swell magnet, so it's converting more than Dee Why but staying a size band under Long Reef — 4–7ft is right in the range you actually enjoy. North Curly corner holds shape best and cuts the sweep. With this much energy running, pick one bank and keep re-lining rather than drifting down the beach.

manly.window: 6:20–11am, the longest clean window of the four. AM sizes 3–4ft.
alerts: Smallest of the four — the S angle mostly misses here

tip.label: The soft option today
tip.text: North Steyne is sheltered from 169°, so it's picking up 3–4ft where Long Reef is 6–10ft. That's not the day for it when everything is genuinely offshore and Dee Why is Fair–Good — this is your fallback if the Point looks like a mess on the cam. Backside on the North Steyne lefts, frontside at the Queenscliff end.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: Your first weekend day and the biggest energy of the three — 720 kJ through the morning. Same script as today: light SW–WSW offshore to about 11am, then onshore from midday. High tide 8:48am. Fair–Good early at Dee Why, Fair everywhere else, so the 8–11am block is the whole session.

dee-why.window: 8–11am is the sweet spot — 4–6ft, offshore SW, and the push to the 8:48am high. Fair–Good rating holds until about 11am then drops to Fair.
alerts: Onshore from midday — nothing worth having after 11:30am

long-reef.window: Dawn to 10am. Still the size magnet at 5–8ft in the morning; Surfline has it Fair all day.
alerts: Backing off from today but still well overhead on the sets

curl-curl.window: 8–11am, North Curly corner. Consistent Fair through the day, best while the SW holds.

manly.window: Morning; 3–4ft AM. Cleanest but smallest of the four again.

days.label: Weekend
days.note: Saturday is the bigger, more powerful day (720 kJ, 4–6ft at Dee Why). Sunday drops hard — 203 kJ and 3–4ft — but Surfline calls it the cleanest AM of the three: 'AM window of clean head high surf, then light onshores.' Figures below are Sunday's, since Saturday has its own tab. Sunday high tide 9:23am, right inside your 10am–12pm slot. If you only surf one weekend day for size, take Saturday; if you want shape and a relaxed mid-morning, take Sunday.

dee-why.window: Sun: 8–11am on the push to the 9:23am high, 3–4ft. Light onshores later but similar size. Point rights on the drop.
alerts: Energy falls from 720 kJ Saturday to 203 kJ Sunday — much softer, groveller territory

long-reef.window: Sun morning. Still the biggest of the four at 4–6ft, and the only one Surfline nudges to Fair–Good — the residual S swell keeps feeding the reef after it's gone everywhere else.

curl-curl.window: Sun mid-morning, North Curly corner. Fair–Good early — arguably the best size/shape trade of the day.

manly.window: Sun: small. 2–3ft and dropping to Poor–Fair by afternoon — only worth it if you want an easy longboard-ish session.
alerts: Smallest and weakest option of the weekend
